# HEARTz: Product Reference

HEARTz is a free browser-based sound workspace. Short playable samples are available at https://heartz.app/ without registration. The full workspace at https://app.heartz.app/ requires an account through Firebase email/password or Google sign-in.

## Suitable uses

- Retuning a supported WAV or FLAC file locally without uploading the source audio.
- Configuring a tone, such as 432 Hz or 528 Hz, and choosing supported binaural or modulation parameters.
- Exploring procedural brown, pink or white noise and guided sound textures according to personal listening preferences.
- Saving supported configurations for later use in the same browser, and using the export controls available in the relevant tool.

## Converter

Input supports specified WAV and FLAC formats, not arbitrary audio formats or MP3. Supported sources are mono/stereo at 44.1, 48, 88.2 or 96 kHz: WAV PCM16/24/32 or Float32, and FLAC 16/24/32-bit. Browser memory, file size and available file-saving capabilities can limit an operation even when its format is supported.

The user supplies the source and target A4 tuning references. A4 = 440 Hz to A4 = 432 Hz applies a pitch ratio of 432/440, approximately -31.77 cents. Natural resampling also slows tempo and increases duration by approximately 1.85%, subject to frame rounding. It does not turn every frequency in a song into 432 Hz or preserve tempo independently.

Export options are uncompressed WAV PCM16, PCM24 or Float32 at a selected 44.1, 48, 88.2 or 96 kHz. The inspected UI defaults to PCM24 / 48 kHz. Output settings are separate from the playback device's runtime sample rate. Resampling changes samples; an uncompressed output container is not a promise of unchanged source samples or zero artifacts.

## Frequency Lab and Guided

Frequency Lab provides controls with 0.01 Hz frequency resolution. This is a control resolution, not a guarantee of physical output accuracy. Carrier ranges depend on the selected range and runtime sample rate; direct subsonic playback is restricted.

A binaural difference is the difference between separate left and right carrier tones. A 7.83 Hz difference is not a direct 7.83 Hz audible carrier. Use stereo headphones to deliver the separate channels to each ear.

Guided offers combinations of procedural tones, noise, pads and drones. Ocean-like textures are procedural sound, not a claim of recorded ocean audio. Brown or pink noise may be combined with a tone or binaural layer; the noise color and binaural parameters are separate features.

## Accounts, local storage and privacy

Selected source audio is decoded and processed locally; HEARTz does not upload it for conversion or add it to the account library. Firebase Authentication handles account sign-in. The website and account services still make network requests.

My library stores supported recipes and configurations for the signed-in account in the current browser profile. It does not store generated audio tracks or synchronize across devices. Export available settings backups before clearing browser data or changing devices. See https://heartz.app/privacy for current service and analytics details.

Local audio processing does not imply that first load, sign-in or every application function works offline.

## Samples and devices

The landing plays short WAV samples with waveform visualization, including an approximately three-second 440/432 comparison. It is distinct from synthesizing a custom session in the application. Audio starts after a user action. Conversion time depends on the source, device, browser and selected settings.

Mobile layouts support the main tools; larger conversions can be limited by memory or browser file-saving capabilities. HEARTz does not certify downstream Bluetooth processing or guarantee background playback on every phone. Start at a comfortable low volume and stop if listening feels uncomfortable.
